options.text: The gate stops it, because a delete outside the project is always denied.
options.why: Tempting. The gate has that rule only if the board sets it. This board only asks.

options.text: The person approves it without reading, because ten yeses came first.
options.why: Right. Repeated prompts train the person to approve, and nothing in the gate says the eleventh ask is different.

options.text: The wall in the delete tool stops it.
options.why: Tempting. The wall guards paths in the file tools; the approval is decided before the tool runs.

outcome: The person approved the eleventh ask without reading it, and the delete ran. The run still passed its tests.
question: After ten harmless prompts, the eleventh ask is a delete outside the project. The person has said yes ten times. What happens?

options.text: In run_tool(), before the tool's function is called.
options.why: Right. The verdict comes first; only then does the tool run.

options.text: After the tool has run, to check the result.
options.why: Tempting and wrong. A gate after the run cannot stop the run.

options.text: In the system prompt, as a rule for the model.
options.why: Tempting. A rule in the prompt is words the model may ignore; the gate is code the harness runs.

question: Where in Rein does the gate run?

options.text: allow, because it starts with an allow-listed command.
options.why: Tempting. The prefix matches, but the chaining check finds &&, so it is not allow-listed.

options.text: ask, because a chained command is not on the allow-list.
options.why: Right. The chaining check sends it to the person.

options.text: deny, because it has two commands.
options.why: Tempting and wrong. Only the deny list denies; a second command alone asks.

question: run_command gets python test_calc.py && echo ok. Which decision does decide() return?

options.text: The allow list, so a known test command runs at once.
options.why: Tempting. Deny rules come first, so a command that matches both is denied.

options.text: The deny list, which denies a match before anything is allowed.
options.why: Right. Deny rules are checked before allow rules.

options.text: The mode, so auto allows everything.
options.why: Tempting. The mode applies to edits, after the command rules.

question: Which check comes first in decide(), for a run_command?

options.text: The gate, which should have asked.
options.why: Tempting. The gate allowed the kind of action; a read-only tool is never asked about.

options.text: The wall inside read_file, which checks the path before it reads.
options.why: Right. The gate decides whether a kind of action is allowed; the wall decides which files the tool can touch.
Tempting. Words guide the model; they do not stop a read the code allows.

question: The gate allows read_file because it is read-only. The model reads ../rein.py. What stops the read?

options.text: allow, because the request was polite and the model is trusted.
options.why: Tempting and wrong. Politeness is not a permission; the command matches the deny list.

options.text: deny, with the reason, and the model is told not to retry the same call.
options.why: Right. The reason goes back as an error, and the denial stays for the run.

options.text: ask, so the person decides about the cleanup.
options.why: Tempting. Deny rules come before the ask; a matched destructive command is refused outright.
